THIS WEEK IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT

Weston's Community Development Authority voted to pay off major bond debt early after closing a tax-increment district that added $354 million in assessed value, while Kronenwetter's Village Board approved a rezoning and green-lit a new community fundraiser.

  • The Village of Weston CDA voted unanimously to redeem its 2017A lease revenue bonds in full, eliminating debt payments that had been scheduled to run through 2031.
  • Weston's CDA also directed staff to bring the question of the authority's future role — including potential disbandment — to the Village Board's next monthly meeting.
  • Kronenwetter's Village Board approved rezoning Marathon County Highway Department property to M2 General Industrial, clearing the way for the county to proceed with facility development.
  • Kronenwetter's board approved a Bushka Park 5K/3K run/walk fundraiser for September 12, 2026, and authorized matching a $5,000 parks grant to support it.
  • Kronenwetter's board gave consensus to move forward on a zero-lot line ordinance change, directing staff and the Plan Commission to draft amendments modeled on neighboring communities.
  • Kronenwetter's CLIPP Committee is set to consider a temporary moratorium on data center development applications and discuss a potential oak wilt ordinance at its Monday meeting.

Coming up: The Wausau School Board meets Monday for both a special meeting and workshop — starting at 5 p.m. — to take up teacher salary schedules, employee handbook updates, and a review of school perceptions survey results that could inform future referendum discussions. Also Monday, Kronenwetter's CLIPP Committee convenes at 6 p.m. to weigh the data center moratorium and oak wilt ordinance, and Marathon County's Health & Human Services Committee meets Thursday at 5 p.m.
